claims.title: Loss-complete history readout is proposed to give activity-sensitive full Lindblad-channel simulation

status: source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, quantum circuit execution, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.
interface: For time-dependent Lindblad dynamics, the input supplies coherent controlled and inverse projected-unitary encodings of the stacked jump map Lstack(t)/g and H(t)/h0 at binary times, with ||Lstack(t)||<=g, ||H(t)||<=h0 and valid Lipschitz constants ell_L, ell_H. No commutation, gap or mixing promise is made. For one unknown input rho, including reference entanglement, define nu_rho=integral_0^T Tr[Lstack(t)^dagger Lstack(t) rho(t)]dt in this supplied jump representation; 0<=nu_rho<=g^2 T. The response proposes a channel with diamond error <=epsilon, expected queries O-tilde(1+g sqrt(T(1+nu_rho))+h0 T) without receiving/estimating nu_rho, and worst-case queries O-tilde(1+(g^2+h0)T). This is an adaptive execution guarantee, not an improved fixed-length worst-case bound or normalized rare-trajectory preparation.
limits: Recover the prior compiler and exact imported simulation/amplification/fallback theorems; independently reconstruct readout implementation, discretization, adaptive instrument error and expected-versus-worst-case accounting. Replay algebraic diagnostics separately, then implement a complete circuit in the promised oracle model before claiming demonstrated capability.
